title: Accounts Assistant
description:
We are recruiting for an Accounts Assistant to join a finance team. This is a varied role supporting the day-to-day financial operations, ensuring accurate financial records, efficient payment processing and effective budget monitoring.

Key Responsibilities
- Process supplier invoices, purchase orders and payments.
- Manage purchase and sales ledger activities.
- Raise invoices and monitor outstanding payments.
- Reconcile bank accounts and online payment systems.
- Investigate financial discrepancies and resolve supplier queries.
- Assist with budget preparation, monitoring and financial reporting.
- Monitor expenditure and highlight potential overspending.
- Obtain quotations and maintain purchasing records.
- Submit VAT returns and support internal and external audits.
- Maintain accurate financial records and ensure compliance with financial procedures and regulations.
- Handle confidential financial information professionally.

Skills and Experience
- Previous experience in an accounts or finance administration role.
- Knowledge of purchase ledger, sales ledger and bank reconciliations.
- Strong numerical skills and attention to detail.
- Excellent organisational and communication skills.
- Confident using accounting software, ideally QuickBooks.
- Ability to work independently, manage priorities and maintain confidentiality.

This role would suit an organised and proactive finance professional looking for a varied accounts position.

title: Accounts Payable Assistant
description:
Location: Thame, Oxfordshire
Salary: £25,000-£30,000 per annum, depending on experience
Contract: Permanent, Full-Time

About the Company

Wade Macdonald is delighted to be recruiting exclusively for an Accounts Payable Assistant to join a well-established and growing SME within the Business Services sector.

Our client prides itself on its welcoming, relaxed and non-corporate environment, with a friendly finance team and excellent employee retention.

This is an opportunity to join a business where people genuinely enjoy working together and where a positive attitude and dependable approach are highly valued.

The Role

Working within a close-knit finance team, you will be responsible for supporting the day-to-day accounts payable function.

Key responsibilities include:
- Processing and coding supplier invoices accurately and efficiently.
- Maintaining purchase ledger records and resolving invoice queries.
- Processing and reconciling employee expenses.
- Managing company credit card transactions and reconciliations.
- Supporting foreign currency invoices and transactions, particularly relating to suppliers in China and the Far East.
- Liaising with suppliers and colleagues to resolve discrepancies.
- Supporting the wider finance team with general accounting and administrative duties.

About You

We are looking for someone who is organised, approachable and takes pride in delivering accurate work.

You may already have experience in accounts payable or purchase ledger and be looking for a stable, enjoyable working environment. Equally, you may have some finance or administrative experience and be keen to develop your skills further.

Ideally, you will offer:
- Previous experience in accounts payable, purchase ledger, finance administration or a similar environment, or a genuine interest in developing within finance.
- Strong attention to detail and good organisational skills.
- A comfortable working knowledge of Excel and financial systems.
- Good communication skills and a friendly, collaborative approach.
- Reliability, consistency and a willingness to support colleagues.
- A positive attitude towards routine transactional accounting work.

AAT qualifications or studies would be welcomed but are not essential. Previous exposure to foreign currency transactions would also be advantageous.

What's on Offer?
- Salary of £26,000-£30,000, depending on experience.
- A stable, established business with excellent employee retention.
- A friendly, supportive and relaxed working environment.
- A close-knit finance team with a collaborative culture.
- The opportunity to settle into a valued role for the long term.
- Scope to develop your finance skills, should you wish to.

How to Apply

Whether you're an experienced Accounts Payable professional looking for a positive change of environment or someone keen to build their finance experience, we'd be delighted to hear from you.

Apply today through Wade Macdonald to find out more.

title: Accounts Receivable Assistant - Cash Allocation
description:
Cash Allocation Specialist Didcot (Hybrid) Permanent Up to £30,000

The Opportunity

IN2 Consult is partnering with a market leading business based near Didcot, to recruit a Cash Allocation Specialist into its Accounts Receivable team. This is a busy, high-volume role at the centre of the order-to-cash process. You will make sure customer receipts are matched, posted and reconciled accurately and on time, so the sales ledger always shows a true picture of what the business is owed.

Key Responsibilities
- Allocate daily customer receipts from BACS, CHAPS, card and cheque payments against open invoices on the sales ledger
- Match remittance advices to payments, investigating and resolving unallocated or unidentified cash
- Reconcile customer accounts and clear historic unallocated balances and suspense items
- Post receipts accurately within agreed daily deadlines
- Work with Credit Control to resolve queries, short payments, overpayments and deductions
- Raise and process customer refunds and credit notes in line with approval controls
- Support the daily bank reconciliation and month-end close, including aged debt reporting
- Contact customers and internal teams to get missing remittance information
- Identify process improvements that cut unallocated cash and speed up allocation

About You
- Previous experience in cash allocation, cash posting, sales ledger or accounts receivable
- Comfortable working through high transaction volumes quickly without losing accuracy
- Good working knowledge of Excel (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables, filters)
- Experience with various ERP systems
- Strong attention to detail with a methodical, problem-solving approach
- Confident communicator, by phone and email, with customers and colleagues
- Able to prioritise a daily workload against firm deadlines

Desirable: AAT studier or interest in studying, shared service centre experience, multi-currency or multi-entity allocation.

title: Finance Administrator
description:
Finance Administrator

Tech Professionals Ltd is a specialist engineering and project support recruitment business, supplying engineers, technicians and skilled professionals across the offshore, subsea and maritime sectors.

We are looking for a detail-driven Finance Administrator to join our team and provide essential support across payroll, invoicing, data management and general finance administration.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator looking to develop their career within finance, gaining valuable hands-on experience across payroll, invoicing, banking and accounts within a growing specialist business.

The Role

As Finance Administrator, you will play an important role in ensuring our financial and payroll processes are accurate, timely and well organised.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Managing, reviewing and validating financial and operational data using Excel
- Supporting the monthly payroll process, including checking timesheets, expenses and contractor information
- Using Xero to prepare and generate client invoices
- Preparing BACS payment files and maintaining accurate banking records
- Reviewing contractor and client contracts to ensure rates are correctly applied for billing and payroll
- Checking data for accuracy and resolving discrepancies where required
- Supporting the wider finance and administration function with general duties as needed
- Working to monthly deadlines while maintaining a high level of accuracy

Skills & Experience

We are looking for someone who is organised, reliable and comfortable working with numbers and detailed information.

You will ideally have:
- Strong Excel skills, with confidence using formulas and working with data
- Previous experience in an administrative role
- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks
- The ability to work to deadlines, particularly around monthly payroll
- Good communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving
- Previous experience with payroll, invoicing, accounts or Xero would be advantageous, but is not essential

Why Join Us?

This is a great opportunity to develop your finance experience within a specialist and growing recruitment business. You will gain exposure to a broad range of finance activities while working closely with the wider team.

If you are an organised administrator with strong Excel skills and an interest in developing a career in finance, we would love to hear from you.

title: HR and Payroll Officer
description:
HR and Payroll Officer

Are you an organised and people-focused HR professional with payroll experience who enjoys delivering excellent service and building strong working relationships

We are seeking an enthusiastic HR and Payroll Officer to join the Human Resources team in this full-time, permanent role.

This role offers the opportunity to work across the full employee lifecycle while building expertise in both HR and payroll. It is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing attention to detail with relationship-building and who takes pride in delivering a high-quality service.

Position: HR & Payroll Officer

Location: Kidlington, Oxford/hybrid

Hours: Full-time, 37 hours per week

Salary: £37,751.95 £40,655.94 per annum

Contract: Permanent

Closing Date: Midnight on Tuesday 18 November 2026. Interviews will take place at Church House, Oxford: Friday 27 November 2026

The Role

You will join the Human Resources team, playing a key role in supporting employees, clergy, managers and senior leaders across the Diocese. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to meaningful work, ensuring people are supported through efficient payroll, recruitment, learning and development, and employee lifecycle processes.

This is a varied and rewarding role within a professional and collaborative HR team that supports both the Diocesan Board of Finance and Diocesan Board of Education. You will provide reliable, confidential and people-centred HR and payroll support that helps employees, clergy and leaders do their best work.

You will also play a key role in delivering recruitment and onboarding activities, be the first point of contact for payroll-related matters and will help maintain robust controls and ensure compliance with statutory and organisational requirements.

About You

We are looking for an experienced HR and payroll professional who is highly organised, accurate and customer-focused, with a passion for providing excellent support and advice. You will be comfortable managing multiple priorities, handling sensitive information with discretion and working collaboratively with a wide range of stakeholders.

You will bring experience of HR administration and payroll processing within a busy organisational environment, together with strong communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving.

You will also have:
- Sound knowledge of generalist HR practices and payroll administration.
- Up-to-date knowledge of UK employment legislation and HMRC requirements relating to payroll, tax and statutory payments.
- Experience supporting recruitment, onboarding, learning and development, employee relations and performance management activities.
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications, and experience using HR management systems and payroll systems.
- High levels of accuracy and attention to detail, particularly when working with payroll and employee data and maintaining accurate employee records.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.

A CIPD and/or CIPP qualification or membership would be advantageous, although applications are welcomed from candidates with transferable skills and experience.

You do not need to be a practising Christian to work here. Around half of staff are not practising Christians, but all are comfortable working within the Christian ethos and values that underpin the organisation s work.

The successful candidate must have the right to live and work in the United Kingdom. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for interviews. We are particularly keen to receive applications from UK Minority Ethnic / Global Majority heritage and disabled candidates, who are currently underrepresented.

You may have experience in other areas such as HR, Human Resources, Personnel, People, HR Officer, Human Resources Officer, Personnel Officer, People Officer, Payroll, Payroll Officer, Payroll Assistant, HR Assistant, Finance Officer, Finance Assistant, HR and Finance, HR and Payroll.

Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client, Not For Profit People.

description:
Competitive Salary Flexible & Hybrid Working Excellent Benefits

We are currently recruiting for an experienced Payroll Administrator to join a well-established and forward-thinking professional services firm for a fixed 12 month contract.

- Previous experience processing weekly and monthly payrolls, preferably from start to finish.
- A good understanding of HMRC payroll requirements and RTI submissions.

title: Payroll Administrator (12 Month Fixed Term Maternity Cover)
description:
Payroll Administrator (12 Month Fixed Term Maternity Cover)

About Verallo

Verallo is an established and growing accountancy and tax advisory firm supporting ambitious business owners, high net worth individuals and international groups. Built on strong client relationships and technical excellence, we combine the stability of a well run practice with the energy and ambition of a modern advisory firm.

We pride ourselves on delivering more than compliance. We build long term partnerships with our clients, providing insight and financial clarity that helps them make confident decisions and achieve their goals.

We are seeking an experienced Payroll Administrator who wants to do more than process transactions. This role offers genuine client interaction and responsibility, and the chance to become a trusted part of our clients' finance function rather than an external service provider.

Our culture is collaborative, supportive and professional. We invest in our people, encourage initiative and recognise contribution. This is a fixed term opportunity to join a forward thinking firm that is investing in its payroll and HR services, with the term and end date confirmed in the contract.

Purpose of the Role

The Payroll Administrator ensures client and internal payrolls are processed accurately and on time throughout a period of cover. The role protects the standard our clients expect and offers real exposure to a firm that is investing in its payroll and HR services.

Core Responsibilities

1. Client Payroll Services
- Processing allocated client payrolls on a weekly and monthly basis, from receipt of data through to payslips, RTI submissions and client reporting
- Managing pension administration for allocated clients, including auto enrolment.
- Preparing and submitting monthly CIS returns for allocated clients, within HMRC deadlines
- Preparing and submitting BACS payment files for client net pay and HMRC liabilities
- Handling client payroll queries, escalating complex matters to the relevant manager
- Maintaining clear communication with clients on deadlines and outstanding information

- Processing Verallo's monthly payroll, with final Partner review before submission

- Following documented payroll processes and keeping them current
- Completing a structured handover at the start and end of the term

Key Accountabilities
- Accuracy of payroll: Ensuring all payrolls are calculated and submitted correctly, with checks completed before release.
- Meeting deadlines: Processing every payroll on time each month and flagging risks early.
- Compliance: Keeping up to date with HMRC and pension requirements and applying them consistently.
- Client service: Responding to client queries promptly and professionally.
- Continuity: Documenting work so the service runs without disruption at handover and return.

Cross-Cover Expectations
- Providing basic payroll cover for the admin team during absence where processes are documented

Remuneration Package
- £35 - £40k, subject to experience
- Flexible and hybrid working arrangements, including flexitime and working from home
